articles.title: Keeping parking permit evidence when an online portal is unavailable
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for keeping parking permit evidence when an online portal is unavailable.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about keeping parking permit evidence when an online portal is unavailable, showing the three concepts Save reference, Check rules, Contact issuer. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Save reference · Check rules · Contact issuer. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: Parking permission may depend on a specific vehicle, zone and date. A saved confirmation does not prove that an entitlement is currently valid. Record the issuing authority and permit reference privately rather than publishing vehicle identifiers.
If an online renewal fails, note the displayed error and check whether a payment was confirmed before trying again. An unavailable portal does not automatically suspend parking restrictions.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Keep an official contact route and a securely stored confirmation. Check current on-street signs before relying on an alternative parking space.
Use the issuer's published enquiry or appeal process where appropriate. Keep correspondence and update your record when an outcome is confirmed.

articles.title: Reporting an unreadable or missing street-name sign
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for reporting an unreadable or missing street-name sign.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about reporting an unreadable or missing street-name sign, showing the three concepts Locate safely, Describe fault, Report. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Locate safely · Describe fault · Report. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: A damaged or missing street-name sign can make navigation and deliveries harder, especially where nearby streets have similar names. Identify the public junction and describe the problem.
Note whether the plate is absent, rotated, obstructed or unreadable. Observe from a safe pedestrian position; do not enter traffic to inspect or photograph it.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Find the relevant local authority's street-sign reporting channel. A private road or managed estate may have a different responsible organisation.
For visitors, provide a verified nearby landmark rather than inventing a street name. Retain the report reference and check for an official response later.

articles.title: Recording a local grit-bin problem before cold weather
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for recording a local grit-bin problem before cold weather.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about recording a local grit-bin problem before cold weather, showing the three concepts Identify bin, Note condition, Report. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Identify bin · Note condition · Report. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: Public grit bins may be maintained by different organisations, and their presence does not guarantee that nearby paths will be treated. Record the bin's location and visible identifier.
From a safe position, note obvious damage, obstruction or an apparently empty bin. Do not climb inside, enter a road or assume the contents are available for private use.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Use the responsible council or land manager's reporting channel and keep the reference. Do not assume any material is suitable for every surface.
Plan an accessible alternative for essential journeys when conditions are difficult. Follow current official winter-service information rather than relying on an offline diagram.

articles.title: Preparing a lost-property reference for disrupted journeys
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for preparing a lost-property reference for disrupted journeys.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about preparing a lost-property reference for disrupted journeys, showing the three concepts Record journey, Describe item, Contact operator. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Record journey · Describe item · Contact operator. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: A lost-property enquiry is easier to describe when you know the operator, route, direction, approximate time and boarding or exit point. Record only details you can confirm.
Describe distinctive external features without publishing passcodes, document numbers or financial information. Keep ownership evidence privately for verified requests.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Transport operators and stations may have separate lost-property processes. Save official enquiry contacts ahead of time where practical.
Retain the case number and follow the operator's instructions. Do not travel to an unconfirmed collection point or assume an item has been recovered.

articles.title: Planning for a temporary change to a public building entrance
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for planning for a temporary change to a public building entrance.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about planning for a temporary change to a public building entrance, showing the three concepts Main entrance, Confirm access, Alternative. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Main entrance · Confirm access · Alternative. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: A temporary entrance can change ramp access, door width, opening hours or the route to lifts. A sign saying use another door does not establish step-free access.
Before a necessary visit, identify the venue operator and the specific access features required. Avoid recording a person's private medical details in shared notes.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Ask whether the temporary entrance and the onward route to the intended service meet the traveller's needs. Arrange an alternative appointment if access cannot be confirmed.
Record who confirmed arrangements and when. Temporary works may change again, so retain a fallback contact method for the venue.

articles.title: Responding to an unavailable public drinking-water point
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for responding to an unavailable public drinking-water point.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about responding to an unavailable public drinking-water point, showing the three concepts Check notice, Find alternative, Confirm supply. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Check notice · Find alternative · Confirm supply. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: A drinking fountain can close for maintenance, seasonal operation or other reasons. A closed outlet does not alone prove a wider supply issue.
Read posted notices without handling damaged fittings. Do not use an outlet marked out of service or assume that an unlabelled nearby tap provides drinking water.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Identify more than one legitimate refill option and consider access hours and personal needs. Saved directories may be outdated.
Report visible damage to the operator. If a notice concerns water quality, follow current responsible-authority instructions; an offline article cannot establish safety.

articles.title: Preparing for temporary closure of public bicycle parking
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for preparing for temporary closure of public bicycle parking.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about preparing for temporary closure of public bicycle parking, showing the three concepts Usual stand, Check access, Other stand. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Usual stand · Check access · Other stand. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: Cycle stands may be removed or fenced off during works and events. A marked cycle route does not guarantee parking at the destination.
Note the extent of the restriction without moving barriers or entering a work area. Identify permitted alternatives before an essential journey.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Choose a place that does not obstruct pavements, entrances or accessible routes. Do not assume a tree, railing or road sign is an authorised parking point.
Check locking facilities, access hours and operator conditions. Save official contact information and revisit it when restrictions change.

articles.title: Organising household information about planned noisy street works
articles.summary: An offline planning reference for organising household information about planned noisy street works.

visual.alt: An original offline planning diagram about organising household information about planned noisy street works, showing the three concepts Record notice, Plan access, Check updates. It is not a live status map.
visual.caption: Planning reference: Record notice · Plan access · Check updates. Check current official information.

sections.title: Recognise and record the issue
paragraphs: A works notice may give expected dates and hours, but programmes can change. Record the issuer, location, reference and date checked.
Separate confirmed access restrictions from guesses about noise. Consider effects on deliveries, work, school journeys and mobility needs without publishing household routines.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Contact the works promoter or highway authority about access and notifications. Different organisations may handle different questions.
Keep responses and update the household plan when works change. Do not interfere with barriers or equipment; follow current site instructions.
